book.title: Lider Yok Köle Yok (The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari)
book.author: Robin Sharma

confidence_note: Julian Mantle's story is from The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari (1997); the input title appears to be mismatched with this book. The book is a fable. Well-attested details: Julian is a celebrated, hard-driving trial lawyer with a red Ferrari; he collapses from a heart attack in a courtroom; he sells his possessions and travels to India and the Himalayas, where he learns from the Sages of Sivana; he returns transformed to share their wisdom with the narrator, a former colleague. The TR text's 'monastery' is loose; he found the sages in the mountains. The exact duration of his absence is omitted because it was not verified. The 'true leadership starts with leading yourself' framing is a summary of the book's theme of self-mastery, not a quote.
facts: Julian Mantle is a famous, highly paid trial lawyer with a mansion and a red Ferrari, working punishing hours.
In the middle of a courtroom he collapses from a heart attack.
He gives up his law practice, sells his possessions including the Ferrari, and travels to India in search of a different way to live.
In the Himalayas he finds the Sages of Sivana and learns their teachings on mastering the mind, purpose and living well.
Julian later reappears in the office of the narrator, a former colleague, looking so changed and youthful that he is not recognised at first, and passes the sages' teachings on to him.
Sharma presents the story as a fable: the lesson is that outward success without inner mastery and balance proved hollow.
tension: Julian had everything that looks like success, and it took a collapse in the courtroom to show him that it was not working.
opening_idea: Open on a star lawyer in full flow before a packed courtroom, and pause just before his body stops cooperating.

lessons.idea: External markers of success can hide a way of living that is not sustainable.
lessons.anchor: The Ferrari and the fame, ending in a courtroom heart attack.

lessons.idea: Real change often needs a deliberate break from the setting that sustained the old habits.
lessons.anchor: Julian selling his possessions and travelling to the Himalayas.

lessons.idea: What someone learns about living well becomes more valuable once it is passed on.
lessons.anchor: Julian returning to teach the narrator what the sages taught him.

reflect: Is there something in your life that looks good from the outside but is costing you more than you admit?
What warning signs do you tend to ignore until something forces you to stop?
reflect_final: This week, name one thing you have been putting off because of work, such as sleep, a check-up or time with someone, and book one concrete time for it.

use_cases.situation: A colleague is proud of working every weekend and brushes off tiredness.
use_cases.move: Ask them, without lecturing, what their week would look like if they had to protect their health first.

use_cases.situation: You are about to accept one more big commitment on top of an already full load.
use_cases.move: Remember that Julian's success only looked complete until the courtroom collapse; before saying yes, write down what you would have to give up to make room, and decide based on that list.

use_cases.situation: Friends are comparing cars, promotions and holidays over dinner.
use_cases.move: Share Julian Mantle's story and ask what each person would keep if they had to sell their own 'Ferrari'.

pocket_idea: Julian sold the Ferrari only after a courtroom collapse: notice what your own 'Ferrari' is costing you before your body sends the bill.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: A star lawyer had a heart attack in court and then sold his Ferrari to go and look for sages in the Himalayas.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Julian Mantle, a wealthy trial lawyer with a red Ferrari, collapses in court, sells everything, finds the Sages of Sivana in the Himalayas and returns so changed his old colleague barely recognises him.
conversation_variants.question_idea: Ask whether they have ever had a moment when something that looked like success suddenly felt wrong.
conversation_variants.key_contrast_idea: A life that looked perfect from outside versus one that was actually working.
